options: Floats are stored in binary, and 0.1 has no exact binary form
It is a bug fixed in Python 3.14
rationales: Python does not round the sum at all - it shows the nearest binary value exactly.
It is not a bug: Python 3.14.4 prints the same result, because the cause is binary representation.

items.q: What type of value does input() return when the user types 42?
rationales: input() never converts: digits arrive as text until int() converts them.
Python cannot know intent; input() always returns a string.
Python does not convert 42 to text silently; you must write str(42).
+ never discards its left operand; the operation fails instead.

items.q: Which is the modern way to build 'Hello, Alice!' from name = 'Alice'?
rationales: Concatenation works, but every value must already be a string and it is harder to read; f-strings are the current idiom (PEP 701).
* repeats a string by an integer; a string name cannot be a repeat count.
